recommendedTextbook.title: Basic Science for Junior Secondary Schools 1 (UBE Revised 5th Edition)
recommendedTextbook.author: F.O.C. Ndu, P. Asun, J.O. Aina
recommendedTextbook.approvedBy: NERDC & Lagos State Ministry of Basic Education

topics.topic: Artificial Intelligence & Sensor Robotics in Agriculture
subtopics: Automated soil moisture sensors in Nigerian farms
Drone-assisted crop inspection and yield prediction
objectives: Identify 2 agricultural robotic sensors used in Nigeria
Differentiate between manual irrigation and automated sensor systems

topics.topic: Living Things: Differences Between Plants and Animals
subtopics: Morphological differences between plants and animals
Modes of nutrition (autotrophic vs heterotrophic)
Locomotion vs movement in plants and animals
objectives: List 5 structural differences between plants and animals
Explain how green plants manufacture food via photosynthesis
Illustrate leaf structure using hibiscus leaves collected locally

topics.topic: Living Things: Habitat, Ecology & Climate Resilience in Nigeria
subtopics: Terrestrial and aquatic ecological habitats in Nigeria (Mangrove, Rainforest, Sahel)
Adaptive features of indigenous plants and animals to extreme weather
Climate change mitigation and environmental hygiene in school communities
objectives: Identify 3 major Nigerian ecological zones and their characteristic flora/fauna.
Describe 4 structural adaptations of desert and mangrove organisms.
Propose 2 practical tree planting actions to combat desertification and erosion.

topics.topic: Family Health II: Human Puberty and Adolescent Development
subtopics: Meaning of puberty and adolescence
Physical and emotional changes in adolescent boys and girls
Menstruation and menstrual hygiene management
objectives: Explain puberty changes in boys (voice breaking, facial hair) and girls (breast development, menstruation)
State menstrual hygiene protocols for adolescent girls
Discuss emotional self-regulation during adolescent transitions

subtopics: Classes of food: carbohydrates, proteins, fats/oils, vitamins, mineral salts, water
Local Nigerian sources of each food class (yam, beans, palm oil, bitter leaf)
Balanced diet and deficiency diseases (kwashiorkor, scurvy, rickets)
objectives: Identify the six statutory classes of food
Map everyday Nigerian meals (e.g. jollof rice, beans and dodo) to nutrients
Explain symptoms and prevention of nutritional deficiencies in children

topics.topic: Environmental Pollution I: Air and Water Pollution
subtopics: Meaning of pollution and pollutants
Causes of air pollution (exhaust fumes from Danfo buses, generator smoke, refuse burning)
Water pollution causes (dumping plastics, sewage, industrial effluents into Lagos Lagoon)
objectives: Define pollution and distinguish between air and water pollutants
List health hazards of generator exhaust fumes (carbon monoxide poisoning)
Propose community-based waste disposal solutions to preserve water sources

subtopics: Diagnostic review of Weeks 1-6 concepts
Mid-term written assessment
Targeted remediation for struggling learners
objectives: Assess pupil mastery of living things, hygiene, puberty, nutrition, and pollution
Identify conceptual gaps and provide tiered remediation exercises

topics.topic: Environmental Pollution II: Soil and Noise Pollution
subtopics: Soil pollution causes (non-biodegradable plastics, chemical pesticides)
Noise pollution sources (loudspeakers, market clamor, sirens)
Prevention and control of environmental degradation
objectives: Explain harmful effects of polythene nylon bags on soil fertility
State hearing damage thresholds caused by prolonged generator noise
Formulate classroom environmental action pledges

topics.topic: Energy: Meaning, Forms and Sources of Energy
subtopics: Definition of energy and measurement unit (Joules)
Forms of energy (kinetic, potential, thermal, light, chemical, electrical, sound)
Renewable energy vs non-renewable energy (solar vs crude oil)
objectives: Define energy and state its S.I. unit
Differentiate between kinetic and potential energy with everyday Nigerian examples
Compare solar power with fossil fuel generation in Nigerian households

topics.topic: Force: Meaning, Types and Effects of Force
subtopics: Meaning of force as a push or a pull (unit: Newton)
Contact forces (friction, tension, push/pull)
Non-contact forces (gravitational force, magnetic force, electrostatic force)
objectives: Define force and demonstrate push and pull actions
Differentiate contact from non-contact forces
Measure force using a spring balance in the school laboratory

topics.topic: Gravitational Pull and Friction in Daily Life
subtopics: Earth gravitational attraction
Meaning and causes of friction
Advantages and disadvantages of friction on Nigerian highways
objectives: Explain why unsupported objects fall toward the Earth
List 3 advantages and 3 disadvantages of friction
Describe methods of reducing friction (lubrication, ball bearings)

topics.topic: The Solar System: Sun, Planets and Earth in Space
subtopics: Components of the solar system (the Sun and 8 planets)
Position of Earth in relation to the Sun
Rotation of the Earth (day and night) and Revolution (seasons)
objectives: Name all eight planets in order of distance from the Sun
Demonstrate how Earth rotation causes day and night using a globe and torchlight
Explain why Nigeria experiences rainy and dry seasons rather than snowfall

subtopics: Termly syllabus review across all 12 weeks
Terminal examination moderation and broadsheet compilation
objectives: Demonstrate holistic mastery of JSS 1 Basic Science Term 1 curriculum
